title: AMC Renews 'Interview With the Vampire' for Season 4 as 'Queen of the Damned'
excerpt: The Anne Rice adaptation shifts focus to ancient vampire Akasha, with Sheila Atim taking center stage and playwright Hannah Moscovitch stepping in as showrunner.
body:
• AMC announced at San Diego Comic-Con on July 24 that Interview With the Vampire has been renewed for a fourth season, titled Anne Rice's Queen of the Damned.
  • Sheila Atim's Akasha, the ancient queen of all vampires, will take center stage after being awakened in the Season 3 finale.
  • Hannah Moscovitch replaces Rolin Jones as showrunner, becoming the first woman to helm the franchise.
  • A teaser trailer unveiled at SDCC's Hall H panel featured Atim delivering a fiery monologue as Akasha.

AMC's flagship Anne Rice adaptation has been renewed for a fourth season and will carry a new title: Queen of the Damned. The announcement came during the show's Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, continuing a naming convention that has seen the series rebrand each season to match its source novel.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=q8Oysn9I9K8

The series launched in 2022 as Interview With the Vampire, adapted from Rice's 1976 debut novel. Season 3 rebranded as The Vampire Lestat, tracking the second book in The Vampire Chronicles. Now, Season 4 will draw from Rice's third novel, The Queen of the Damned, centering on Akasha — the millennia-old progenitor of all vampires — played by Sheila Atim.

Akasha Takes the Throne

The Season 3 finale, which aired on July 19, ended on a devastating cliffhanger. Sam Reid's Lestat, recording his memoirs in a silk robe, opened a balcony door to reveal a post-apocalyptic New York City — the result of Akasha's awakening triggered by his Montreal concert. That destruction sets the stage for Season 4.

https://x.com/PopBase/status/2080750249744777550

"We can't wait to continue the journey with Queen of the Damned, one of the most iconic stories in Anne Rice's mythology, and watch our established and beloved characters confront Akasha with their world, and ours, very much hanging in the balance."

— Dan McDermott, Chief Content Officer, AMC Global Media

A teaser trailer titled "She Is the Answer" accompanied the announcement. In it, Atim delivers a chilling monologue as Akasha over images of women in protest: "You who have called to me, not knowing my name. You, with your dresses stained, your faces down in the mud. I have heard you." The speech culminates in a command — "Kill them all" — before Akasha declares, "I am the answer."

New Showrunner, Continued Vision

Hannah Moscovitch will serve as showrunner and executive producer on Queen of the Damned, replacing Rolin Jones, who helmed the first three seasons. Moscovitch, a critically acclaimed Canadian playwright known for Sexual Misconduct of the Middle Classes and the Crave TV miniseries Little Bird, was a writer on the first two seasons of Interview With the Vampire and an executive producer on The Vampire Lestat. She specifically wrote the Akasha and Gabriella characters for Season 3.

Jones remains on board as executive producer alongside Mark Johnson and Christopher Rice, the late Anne Rice's son. Jones has previously described Season 3 as "part one of two," suggesting the narrative arc he envisioned will continue under Moscovitch's stewardship.

A Franchise Hitting Its Stride

The renewal arrives with commercial and critical wind at AMC's back. The network noted in a press release that The Vampire Lestat ranks among the highest-rated TV shows of the year on Rotten Tomatoes. The series stars Reid, Jacob Anderson as Louis de Pointe du Lac, Assad Zaman as Armand, Eric Bogosian as Daniel Molloy, Delainey Hayles, and Jennifer Ehle.

In Rice's 1988 novel, Akasha awakens after centuries of dormancy, drawn by Lestat's rock music, and embarks on a global campaign to reshape civilization — slaughtering men and positioning herself as a goddess. The television adaptation has already laid the groundwork with Atim's introduction in Season 3, and the post-apocalyptic finale suggests the show will not shy away from the novel's scale.

What's Next

AMC has not announced a premiere date for Queen of the Damned. All episodes of The Vampire Lestat are streaming on AMC+. The SDCC panel also featured Anderson, Zaman, Bogosian, and Atim alongside producers Johnson and Moscovitch, signaling the core cast will return.

For longtime Vampire Chronicles fans, the adaptation represents a second chance at a faithful screen treatment of Queen of the Damned — the 2002 film starring the late Aaliyah was a commercial disappointment and widely panned by critics and Rice herself. With three seasons of goodwill and a rising star in Atim, AMC's version enters development on considerably stronger footing.
